title: Tapered bulk pricing structure for semantic vectors + rerank surcharge
creator: Mariana Chen
description:
Problem: enterprise customers report unpredictable costs for large batched embedding and rerank workloads. Current per-vector billing + flat batch discount does not reflect diminishing marginal cost across very large bulk jobs, nor does it allow a small premium for compute-heavy re-ranking (cross-encoder) calls.

Goal: design and validate a tapered bulk discount curve for semantic vectors that (a) reduces list-price friction for very large customers, (b) preserves unit economics for typical usage, and (c) introduces a clear, simple rerank surcharge tier for cross-encoder / full-candidate re-ranking requests. The output will be a pricing proposal, evaluation simulations, an experiment plan for a pilot cohort, and a completed QSA/contract checklist for enterprise negotiations.
acceptance_criteria: A documented tapered pricing curve with at least 4 breakpoints (e.g., 0-10M, 10M-100M, 100M-1B, 1B+) and per-vector effective price for each bucket
A separate, explicit rerank surcharge model (either a multiplier or fixed per-call add-on) with cost rationale and sample customer invoices
Simulated revenue and unit-cost impact across 5 archetypal customer profiles using production token distributions
An A/B pilot segmentation plan and rollout criteria (metrics, minimum cohort size, rollback policy)
QSA / contract language template covering billing definitions, rounding/aggregation, and auditability, reviewed with legal and sales ops
comments: 2026-03-04: Initial scoping meeting with Finance (Asha Patel) and Sales Ops (Noah Rivera). Agreed to avoid negative margin in any bucket and to treat rerank as a compute-dense feature.
2026-03-06: Eng asked for latency profiling per-candidate for cross-encoder rerank—ENG-22111 referenced. Liam to get 7-day histograms.

2026-03-09: Ran first batch-econ sim using last 90 days of embeddings traffic. Preliminary finding: 80% of $ volume concentrated in top 2% of customers; tapered discounts materially improve win-rate for those customers but reduce short-term ARR by ~3% unless we tie discounts to commitment/term length.
2026-03-12: Draft PRD uploaded to Confluence (link below). Legal sent initial QSA checklist items; flagged billing auditability and definition of 'vector' vs 'candidate' as negotiation points.
2026-03-14: Sync with Growth to map pilot list (5 prospective customers) and define success metrics: <5% revenue lift loss vs baseline and >15% trial conversion within 60 days.
Follow-ups: finalize pricing math, get engineering cost estimates for rerank compute, and prepare sales negotiation playbook.
notes: Design trade-offs considered: (1) keep list-price simple vs maximize revenue with many micro-buckets, (2) surcharge as multiplier vs per-call fixed line item, (3) link discounts to contractual commit vs open self-serve tier. Recommendation is tapered buckets with commit-linked deeper discounts and an explicit per-rerank multiplier in the short-term pilot.
